title: Voice: read aloud, spoken replies and recall
notes: Read aloud (Status → Voice): the app speaks each line of an open checklist, waits for ✓ Checked, then reads the next. Works offline and in Bluetooth headsets. Speaking rate and voice are selectable.

Voice replies (experimental): after each line the app listens for “checked”, “set”, “repeat”, “skip” or “stop”. What it heard is shown before anything is applied. Needs microphone permission and, on Apple devices, signal.
Say procedure: with voice replies on, a microphone button above each checklist list lets you say a procedure name, for example “engine failure in flight”, and the app opens it.
All of this is off by default; nothing changes unless you turn it on.
Status → Voice has a Test the microphone button that reports exactly what the device says, and the voice bar names the reason when listening fails.
Spoken replies are acted on as soon as the word is heard, without waiting for the end-of-speech pause.
Default speaking rate lowered, with five steps from Slow to Fast; tapping a step plays a sample.
Normal checklists are read in short form: the challenge and the capitalised action only, with bracketed detail left on screen. Can be turned off under Status → Voice.

Listening is more dependable: the microphone stays open for as long as a line is waiting, opens a fraction of a second after the voice finishes, and accepts more ways of saying checked. Cue tones (one when listening, two when accepted) can be turned off.
Confirm a line by saying “checked” or the written response itself, for example “both on” or “idle cutoff”. Other words no longer tick a line.
The microphone now opens while the line is being read, so a reply is caught the moment the voice stops; anything heard before that is ignored. Switchable under Status → Voice.

title: Send to EFB, and Mac window fix
notes: The EFB rows on each Status page are now Send to EFB buttons: they open the share sheet with the file attached, so Copy to OzRWY or Save to Files is one tap. On a computer the file opens in the browser to save from there.
EFB files show a banner saying what they are, with a Share this file button and a link back to the app, so they are not mistaken for the app's own checklist.
On Mac and iPad installs the header now clears the window's close, minimise and zoom buttons.
If an EFB file is requested with no signal, a short message appears instead of the app page.
Version is shown as a plain number (1.7) in the app and in the EFB files; the build code moves to small print.

title: User guide
notes: A user guide explaining installation, the picker and favourites, working through checklists, emergency procedures, the Status page, day and night display, updates, offline use, EFB files and troubleshooting. Linked from the picker and every aircraft's Status page, and available offline.
Fixed: opening the app with signal now reliably loads the newest page on the first launch (a fault in the page fetch meant it could take one extra launch).

title: EFB files inside the app, and release notes
notes: Each aircraft's Status page now has an EFB files section: an interactive single-file checklist and a printable PDF for loading into OzRunways or AvPlan, with instructions.
The update bars now say what changed, with a What's new button. The Status page has a What's new row.
Hot and flooded start branches added to the Maule M-6 and M-7 engine start.

title: 30 aircraft and faster updates
notes: Added GA8 Airvan, Maule M-6-235 and M-7-235, King Air B200, Conquest II, Cessna 310R, 402C, 210M and 210R, Navajo, Chieftain, Malibu, Matrix and PC-12/45.
Opening the app with signal now always fetches the newest build instead of a cached copy.
Update bars are coloured: amber when a new version is waiting, green once applied.

title: Favourites and update awareness
notes: Star an aircraft to pin it under Favourites; the app offers this after three opens.
A bar announces a downloaded update while the app is open and an applied update on the next launch; the Status page shows the version and a manual check.

title: Day and night modes, cockpit colours
notes: Header switch cycles Auto, Day and Night; remembered on the device.
Normal, Abnormal and Emergency tabs coloured green, amber and red; warnings red, cautions amber; next-item marker takes the tab colour.

title: Multi-aircraft app
notes: Aircraft picker with 16 common GA types, progress kept per aircraft, V-speeds page and deep links by aircraft id.

title: C208B offline checklist
notes: First installable version with the Cessna 208B checklists, saved progress and offline use.
